## A — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC07-EXAM, WY-SEC07-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC07-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
sections.markdown:
## B — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants study speed selection, yielding, winter-road control and roundabout procedure from the mapped pages.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
The tires provide the car's contact with the roadway, so road condition strongly affects their grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01

Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
Choose a driving speed that fits the road conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Reduce speed before entering a curve because excessive speed can cause the tires to lose grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
Approach a blind intersection at no more than 15 mph when trees, shrubs or buildings obstruct the side view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A01
Slippery pavement reduces tire grip and requires a lower speed than dry pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A01
For a wet road, the handbook calls for a speed reduction of at least 5 to 10 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A01
On packed snow, reduce speed by at least half. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A01
On ice, reduce speed to a crawl and possibly lower still when vehicles are ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A01
Traveling faster than surrounding traffic creates more passing maneuvers and increases crash exposure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A01
Driving slower than traffic or stopping suddenly can be as dangerous as speeding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A02
Recognize slower vehicles early and change speed gradually rather than slowing abruptly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

## C — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists have the same legal right to use a public roadway, so adjust driving and speed to accommodate their slower movement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A02
At night, keep speed low enough to stop within the distance illuminated ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A02
The handbook's darkness example assumes about 250 feet of clear headlight visibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A02
In that dark-road example, a speed above 55 mph does not allow a stop within the 250-foot illuminated distance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A02
Very heavy rain, a snowstorm or thick fog may reduce forward visibility to no more than 100 feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A02
The handbook says no speed is safe when very heavy rain, a snowstorm or thick fog limits forward sight to 100 feet or less. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A02
When visibility is inadequate, pull off the road and wait for it to improve. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A02
Right-of-way laws specify who must yield when road users cannot proceed at the same time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A02
Watch for drivers who fail to yield and take every possible step to avoid a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A02
Bicycles are treated as vehicles with the rights and responsibilities given to motor-vehicle operators. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A02
At an intersection without signs or signals, yield to a driver approaching from the right regardless of who reaches or enters first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A03
Whenever others may cross or enter your path, check to the sides rather than relying on signs or signals alone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A03
The intersection scan described starts ahead, then left, then right, followed by another look in both directions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A03
Look left early because vehicles approaching from the left are encountered first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A03
At a yield-controlled intersection, check cross traffic before arriving at the intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A03
A yield sign in your lane requires yielding to cross traffic close enough to create danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A03
When turning onto a street or highway, yield to vehicles close enough to pose danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A03
Find a gap, merge into traffic and adjust speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0043]

Misconceptions: A yield rule requires giving way rather than claiming an unconditional right to proceed; four-wheel drive does not eliminate skid risk.
Mnemonics: Recall index: slow, look, yield, gap, signal; this organizer restates the source procedures without supplying an extra priority rule.
Glossary: Recall terms: blind intersection, right of way, black ice, conventional brakes, anti-lock brakes and roundabout.
Dynamic facts: Posted signs govern the listed general limits. Unmapped interstate assignments, vehicle-specific gear advice and exact present applicability remain debt; no contact directory is reproduced.

sections.domain: Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Winter storms can rapidly make Wyoming highways slick and icy. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
On winter roads, move slowly and test the surface only when traffic allows. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
The handbook suggests a light brake touch to observe whether the vehicle slows or swerves when checking a winter surface. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
Ice can remain on bridges, overpasses and shaded surfaces even after sunshine returns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A01
Black ice is difficult to see, so watch for sudden changes from wet pavement to extreme iciness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A02
A thin water layer over thawing ice can make the surface even more slippery. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A02
Start moving on snow or ice with slow, steady acceleration and the front wheels aimed straight ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A02
Four-wheel-drive and front-wheel-drive vehicles generally have better traction but can still skid after abrupt changes in power to the driven wheels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A02
Quickly releasing the accelerator is an example of a power change that can trigger a skid on snow or ice. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
A four-wheel-drive vehicle with a high center of gravity is more likely to roll over during a skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A02
In winter conditions, increase following distance regardless of vehicle type. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A02
The winter following-distance example uses a four-count after the vehicle ahead passes a landmark; reaching it before the count ends means following too closely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A03
Braking technique differs between conventional brakes and anti-lock brakes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A03
Jamming conventional brakes can lock the wheels and lead to a skid. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A03
The handbook's conventional-brake guideline is to pump the brakes about once each second. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A03
Do not pump anti-lock brakes because that action is performed automatically. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A03
Keeping speed down on slippery pavement makes stopping easier and reduces skid risk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

sections.domain: Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts — C2.02
sections.heading: C2 — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Speed, right of way, winter travel and roundabouts
FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A03
If a skid starts, turn gently into it and ease off the accelerator until control returns. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A03
The ground-blizzard advice calls for slow speed and slow steering or braking movements without abrupt actions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A03
If another vehicle spins out on an icy hill, stay in line and wait for a snowplow to clear the route. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A03
When helping at an ice-related crash or slide-off, park well away and be ready to move clear if another vehicle loses control at the same location. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A04
At a four-way stop, the driver who stops first should be allowed to proceed first. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A04
When uncertain at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on the right. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A04
Never insist on priority when doing so risks a crash. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A04
Entering an intersection while violating the speed law forfeits any right of way the driver might otherwise have had. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A05
Traffic circulates slowly and counterclockwise in a roundabout. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A05
Roundabout traffic normally keeps moving except to yield to circulating traffic or people in crosswalks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A05
Approach a roundabout slowly and yield to pedestrians and vehicles already circulating. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A05
For roundabout entry, look left and wait for a gap before merging. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A05
Once circulating in a roundabout, keep moving rather than stopping, subject to the source's yielding exceptions. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R31 | anchor: A05
Signal before leaving a roundabout and yield to pedestrians as you exit. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R32 | anchor: A05
Pedestrians should use only the crosswalks when crossing at a roundabout. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R33 | anchor: A05
The handbook attributes fewer crashes, delays and congestion at roundabouts to moving traffic with fewer stops and starts. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R34 | anchor: A05
The handbook links roundabouts' reduced stopping and starting with lower fuel use and emissions. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0048]
